name: _functional_assert_scalar
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied schema: aten::_functional_assert_scalar(Scalar self, str assert_msg, Tensor dep_token) -> Tensor. All registered schema strings supplied for this operator: aten::_functional_assert_scalar(Scalar self, str assert_msg, Tensor dep_token) -> Tensor. The representative signature is not exclusive: original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, aliasing and mutation contract and must not be narrowed to this one signature. Semantics evidenced by the tests and benchmark: when the Scalar `self` is truthy the operator copies `dep_token` into a fresh tensor that mirrors the token's shape, dtype and device, resolving strided/narrowed/sliced/expanded layouts, empty views, lazy conjugate bits and special values (nan/inf) verbatim, while `dep_token` itself is left unmodified; when `self` is falsy (0, 0.0, -0.0, False, 0j) it raises RuntimeError carrying `assert_msg`, with the empty message replaced by the fallback "Assertion is failed". Schema validation rejects a Tensor or non-number `self`, a non-str `assert_msg` (bytes are accepted natively), and a non-Tensor or missing `dep_token`. Backward is not implemented for the probed float16, bfloat16, float32 and float64 tokens on the active backend: torch.autograd.grad raises RuntimeError('derivative for aten::_functional_assert_scalar is not implemented') and the result carries a <NotImplemented> grad_fn. Only the representative overload is modelled here; the remaining call forms and error cases stay with pytest.
